sections.title: Integration Models
sections.text:
2.1 Integration Models
An integration model is an object used to transfer certain master data objects from SAP
S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS. These integration models use the simplified core inter-
face in the SAP S/4HANA system. The core interface is a real-time data exchange frame-
work using the queued remote function call (qRFC) communication technology.
Typically, there are source and target systems involved in transferring data from an ERP
system to the PP/DS system. Because both ERP and PP/DS are part of the same system in
SAP S/4HANA, the source and destinations are the same for the integration model.
There are two steps involved in transferring the data via the integration model:
1. Create the integration model.
The process starts with creation of an integration model where the basic identifiers,
such as the integration model name, the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization
application name, and the logical systems, are defined. In addition, the selection and
filter criteria for the master data objects are defined.

2 Master Data
44
2. Activate the integration model.
The second step in transferring the master data to embedded PP/DS using the inte-
gration model is the activation of the defined integration model. During the activa-
tion, the data defined in the selection criteria for the integration model is packaged
into the RFC queues and transferred to embedded PP/DS.
We’ll walk through both steps in this section.

sections.title: Create the Integration Model
sections.text:
2.1.1 Create the Integration Model
The creation of an integration model is executed using Transaction CFM1 via menu
path, SAP Menu  Logistics  Central Functions  Supply Chain Planning Interface  Core
Interface Advanced Planner and Optimizer  Integration Model  Create.
As shown in Figure 2.1, the Model Name, Logical System, and APO Application uniquely
identify the integration model. We’ll cover the logical system definition and the tech-
nical details in Chapter 3.
Note
SAP S/4HANA can also be used as the ERP system with the SAP Advanced Planning and
Optimization system. Therefore, the SAP S/4HANA integration model also supports the
creation of an integration model for standalone SAP Advanced Planning and Optimi-
zation systems. In addition, with SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP
S/4HANA, it’s also required to create an integration model for the transfer of data from
the source SAP S/4HANA system to SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for
SAP S/4HANA, where PP/DS is implemented. We’ll cover the details of SAP Digital Supply
Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA in Chapter 9. In this case, the integration
model is created with the logical system defined for the SAP Advanced Planning and
Optimization or the SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA sys-
tem, so you’ll see all the master data objects that can be integrated via the core interface
in the integration model transaction. After SAP S/4HANA is selected as the logical sys-
tem, only the master data objects that still require an integration model in embedded
PP/DS are available for selection in the integration model transaction.
The material-dependent master data objects (e.g., contracts and purchase info records)
and the material-independent master data objects (e.g., setup groups and classes) can
also be transferred to embedded PP/DS from SAP S/4HANA using the integration
model.
After the logical system is entered, and if it’s the one defined for the same SAP S/4HANA
system, the system shows only the master data objects that are transferred through the
integration model. Other master data objects are transferred to embedded PP/DS via
generation reports or by setting the Advanced Planning checkbox in the master data
objects (which we’ll discuss throughout this chapter).

sections.title: Activate the Integration Model
sections.text:
2.1.2 Activate the Integration Model
After the integration model is generated, the model needs to be activated. This step will
process the data and send it to embedded PP/DS from SAP S/4HANA. This step also
maps the data to the PP/DS master data objects.
The activation step fetches all the data from SAP S/4HANA and then executes the map-
ping logic in the core interface. For example, the purchase info records from SAP
S/4HANA are fetched and filled into the corresponding core interface structures.
Within embedded PP/DS, when the queue is processed, the data from SAP S/4HANA is
mapped against the structures of the external procurement relationships in embedded
PP/DS. In addition, the corresponding enhancement spots in SAP S/4HANA and in
embedded PP/DS are evaluated and applied during this process.
The activation of the integration model is executed from Transaction CFM2 via menu
path, SAP Menu  Logistics  Central Functions  Supply Chain Planning Interface  Core
Interface Advanced Planner and Optimizer  Integration Model  Activate.
As shown in Figure 2.4, the integration model name, the logical system, and the applica-
tion are the possible selection options in the integration model activation transaction.
Figure 2.4 Activation of Integration Model Selection Screen
The Special CIF Settings section of the screen provides additional options specific to
material master deactivation and parallel core interface loads. In embedded PP/DS,

2 Master Data
48
there is no integration model for the material masters, so the Log Deactivated Material
Masters option isn’t applicable. The Do Not Issue Warning in Case of Parallel CIF Load
option is also not relevant for the SAP S/4HANA system as there are no integration
model–based data transfers executed for the transaction data.
The Parallelized Transfer section, as shown in Figure 2.4, is used to optimize the perfor-
mance of the data selection from SAP S/4HANA and the processing of data in embed-
ded PP/DS. This can be used when the data to be transferred via one integration model
is huge, and executing this in a single threaded process would take a longer time to pro-
cess. Activating parallel processing and entering the number of processes that can be
used by the system will execute multiple threads for selecting SAP S/4HANA data and
also process the queues in parallel within embedded PP/DS.
Out of the master data and transaction data objects that are supported by the core
interface framework, only the external procurement relationships (info records, con-
tracts, and scheduling agreements) objects are relevant for parallel processing in
embedded PP/DS.
Note
The SAP S/4HANA system can also be used as the ERP system along with a standalone
SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system, or the SAP Digital Supply Chain
Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA. Therefore, certain options, such as the special
core interface settings, are still present in the SAP S/4HANA system to support the data
transfer to a standalone SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system and SAP
Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA via the core interface.
After the selection criteria for the integration model are entered, click the Execute but-
ton. In the next screen, the details of the integration model are displayed, as shown in
Figure 2.5. An integration model can be activated and deactivated any number of times,
so the previous status and the new status that will be executed upon clicking the Start
action are shown in the screen.
Based on the selection, all the relevant integration models are listed in the left side of
the screen, and when you select a specific integration model, the details are loaded on
the right side of the screen. A consistency check can be executed by using the Check
button in this screen. To set the status of the integration model (whether activate or
deactivate), you use the Active/Inactive button.
Tip
In addition to creating and activating the integration model, Transaction CFM4 can be
used to display it as well. Transaction CFM5 can be used to search for the integration
model that a particular master data object is part of. In addition, Transaction CFM7 is
used to delete integration models.

49

sections.title: Locations
sections.text:
2.2 Locations
Figure 2.5 Activation of the Integration Model: Details Screen
All the master data objects transferred from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS are
assigned to model 000 and version 000, which are the active model and version in the
embedded PP/DS system. We’ll cover the details of the model and version in Chapter 3,
along with the technical settings required to work with the integration model. The
technical monitoring of the integration models will be discussed in Chapter 9.
2.2 Locations
In this section, we’ll cover the different location master data types relevant for embed-
ded PP/DS and how this data is transferred into embedded PP/DS from SAP S/4HANA.
In addition, we’ll cover the PP/DS settings that need to be maintained in the location
master data.
In embedded PP/DS, the definition of locations includes plants, material requirements
planning (MRP) areas, vendors, customers, and shipping/receiving points. The struc-
ture of these data objects isn’t the same in SAP S/4HANA because plants and MRP areas
are customizing data, whereas vendors and customers are created as master data. The
PP/DS location master doesn’t differentiate between SAP S/4HANA classification of the
data, such as customizing or master data, and treats the location as a master data object
in embedded PP/DS.
ABAP program /SAPAPO/CREATE_LOCATION is delivered in the SAP S/4HANA system
to transfer the location data from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS. You can use ABAP
program /SAPAPO/UPD_LOC_SP_PL to update the location data in embedded PP/DS
when changes are performed to the corresponding data in SAP S/4HANA.
In ABAP program /SAPAPO/CREATE_LOCATION, the selection of relevant location
data (e.g., plants, MRP areas, shipping points, and business partners representing cus-
tomers and vendors) is entered as shown in Figure 2.6. When this report is executed,
the data is fetched, processed, and sent to embedded PP/DS. Fields such as Create for
Standard Addresses, Create for Std & Delivery Adrs, and Enable Adv. SR aren’t relevant

2 Master Data
50
for embedded PP/DS. These fields are leveraged by other solutions such as embedded
transportation management in the SAP S/4HANA system.
Figure 2.6 Creating PP/DS Locations for Business Partners, Plants, MRP Areas, and Shipping/
Receiving Points
The locations transferred from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS can be edited in
embedded PP/DS to enhance the location master with PP/DS data such as calendars
and resources. The following enhancement options are also available for the integra-
tion of location master data:
 BAdI /SAPAPO/LOC_CREATE
Create business partner locations on saving a business partner.
 BAdI /SAPAPO/LOC_DETAILS
Change the location details.
In the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system, the customer master data is
transferred from the ERP system to SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization as a cus-
tomer location (location type 1010), and the vendors are transferred as a vendor loca-
tion (location type 1011). With SAP S/4HANA, the business partner master data object
© 

51
2.2 Locations
replaces the vendor and customer master data. Therefore, in embedded PP/DS, loca-
tion types 1010 and 1011 are replaced by location type 1021, representing the business
partner master data object.
Although a plant is an organizational structure data object created in the Customizing
of SAP S/4HANA, it’s transferred to embedded PP/DS as a master data element. As
shown in Figure 2.7, the basic information of the plant is defined in the SAP S/4HANA
system.
Figure 2.7 Definition of a Plant in SAP S/4HANA Customizing
After the report for transferring the plant location is executed, the plant location of
location type 1001 (production plant) is created in embedded PP/DS. The basic data
items, such as name, address, time zone, and regions, are transferred to the location
master data. The PP/DS data is maintained in the PP/DS transaction for the location
master. The location master can be accessed from Transaction /SAPAPO/LOC3 or via
menu path, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Master Data  Location  Location. The Loca-
tion and Location Type are entered, as shown in Figure 2.8. Select the Change button to
change and add additional PP/DS information to the location master.

2 Master Data
52
Figure 2.8 PP/DS Location Master Data: Initial Screen
As shown in Figure 2.9, the general data settings, including the administrative data
such as Created and Changed, are in the General tab. The basic data transferred from
SAP S/4HANA is updated in the Address tab.
Figure 2.9 Location Master in Embedded PP/DS
© 

53
2.2 Locations
Note
In embedded PP/DS, all the master data and transaction data items are assigned to a
supply chain model and version. Versions can be created to simulate any planning-
relevant parameters. 000 is the active model, and 000 version is the active version. The
master and transaction data integrated into embedded PP/DS from SAP S/4HANA is
always assigned to the 000 version.
For maintaining the PP/DS calendars, click on the Calendar tab and maintain the Pro-
duction Calendar for scheduling the production activities and the Display Calendar
(PPDS) for controlling the display of the periodic views in PP/DS planning tools such as
the production planning table.
Tip
For creating PP/DS planning calendars, use Transaction /SAPAPO/CALENDAR.
The handling resources in the location master are used by the goods receipt (GR) and
goods issue (GI) processing operations. To support GR/GI processing times assigned in
the product masters, the handling resources must be assigned in the location master.
To maintain the resources, click on the Resources tab, and maintain the handling
resources as shown in Figure 2.10. Resource Inbound is used in scheduling the GR activ-
ities when GR processing is assigned in the material master, and Resource Outbound is
used in scheduling GI activities.
Figure 2.10 PP/DS Location Master: Handling Resource Assignment

2 Master Data
54
The business partner master data is created in SAP S/4HANA, and depending on the
role of the business partner, the role-specific data is added in SAP S/4HANA. Depending
on whether the business partner is a vendor or customer, the same entity acts as a ven-
dor and customer. In embedded PP/DS, the location mater data is used in transaction
data objects. For example, the plant location data is used in in-house manufacturing
orders such as planned orders and production orders, and the vendor location master
data and customer location master data are used in the purchasing documents and
sales documents, respectively. The context for the transaction data is enhanced with
the location master data details in embedded PP/DS.

sections.title: Product Master
sections.text:
2.3 Product Master
In this section, we’ll cover the details of the product master in PP/DS in SAP S/4HANA
and how the material master maintained in the SAP S/4HANA system is transferred to
embedded PP/DS. In the SAP S/4HANA system, the material master holds the informa-
tion about the materials that a company manufactures, procures, and stores in its
premises.
Depending on the usage of the material in the company, different material types are
defined. Based on the type of material, such as raw material, semifinished material, or
finished product, the relevant information is stored in the material master data.

sections.title: Activation of Advanced Planning for Materials
sections.text:
2.3.1 Activation of Advanced Planning for Materials
In the PP/DS component of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, the material
master created in the ERP system must be transferred to the SAP Advanced Planning
and Optimization system via the core interface. In addition, the integration model is
required to transfer the material master to the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimiza-
tion system. Change pointers are also implemented to send the material master
changes to the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system when a change is
made in the ERP system. The material master data in SAP Advanced Planning and Opti-
mization is called the product master, and any product master data from the PP/DS
component of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization is directly maintained in the
SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system. Due to the presence of the core
interface layer between the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization and ERP sys-
tems, there are challenges in monitoring the queues for any errors and correcting them
to ensure the data consistency between the ERP and SAP Advanced Planning and Opti-
mization systems.
In embedded PP/DS, there is no need to create an integration model for the material
master. As PP/DS is part of the SAP S/4HANA core, the material master created in SAP
S/4HANA is available for PP/DS by activating the material for advanced planning. There
is a new view in the SAP S/4HANA material master where the PP/DS-specific master
© 

55
2.3 Product Master
data can be maintained. Therefore, the maintenance of the material master is only pos-
sible from the ERP side transaction within the SAP S/4HANA system, and the PP/DS
product master is a display-only view.
As shown in Figure 2.11, from the material master Transaction MM01 (Create Material)
or Transaction MM02 (Change Material), navigate to the Advanced Planning tab, and
check the Advanced Planning checkbox on the material master. This checkbox immedi-
ately makes the material master available for PP/DS planning upon saving the material
master. In addition, activating Advanced Planning will populate the mandatory fields,
such as the PP Plng Procedure in the material master.
Once you activate the Advanced Planning checkbox and press (Enter), you’ll see that
the Not relevant for planning field is changed to Active for planning. You can activate a
material for advanced planning, but it can be deactivated if planning of the material is
no longer required in PP/DS. In this case, the material is still integrated to embedded
PP/DS, but no planning or changes are possible in PP/DS.
Figure 2.11 Activation of Advanced Planning in SAP S/4HANA Material Master
Any additional PP/DS master data that is relevant for specific planning scenarios
within PP/DS can be maintained in this Advanced Planning tab. As shown in Figure 2.12,
the PP/DS data is stored in SAP S/4HANA material master table MARC. The PP/DS data-
base tables (e.g., table /SAPAPAO/MATLOC) are just a view of the data stored in table MARC,
and they don’t persist the data.

2 Master Data
56
Figure 2.12 PP/DS Fields in SAP S/4HANA Material Master: Table MARC
The activation of advanced planning in the material master assigns the material to the
active PP/DS model and version. The product master can be displayed in the PP/DS
Transaction /SAPAPO/MAT1. This is a display-only view, and no data maintenance is
possible in the PP/DS transaction. All the basic MRP and advanced planning data
objects maintained in the material master are visible in the PP/DS product master, as
shown in Figure 2.13.
Figure 2.13 PP/DS Product Master Data in SAP S/4HANA
© 

57
2.3 Product Master
Note
Direct creation of material in embedded PP/DS isn’t possible for simulation purposes.
Materials are always created and maintained in the ERP transaction and must be acti-
vated for advanced planning.
Materials are created and assigned to a plant in SAP S/4HANA, and the same assign-
ment is available for the PP/DS product master data. Therefore, the location master
data of the plant must be integrated before activating the material for advanced plan-
ning. If an advanced planned material is assigned to an MRP area within the plant, the
material can be planned in the MRP area in PP/DS as well. However, the MRP area
should be integrated as a PP/DS location prior to activation of advanced planning.

sections.title: Deactivation of Advanced Planning for Materials
sections.text:
2.3.2 Deactivation of Advanced Planning for Materials
When a material is activated for advanced planning by setting the Advanced Planning
indicator in the material master, and the material master is saved, in the PP/DS side,
the material and the plant combination is created as a pegging area. Internally, the sys-
tem generated a Global Unique Identifier (GUID) for the material/plant combination
called a peg key, which identifies the pegging area and saves it in SAP liveCache. SAP
liveCache is object-based in-memory storage within the SAP HANA database where the
embedded PP/DS data is replicated, so that the access to such data is faster.
All the transaction data transferred from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS is linked
with the material/plant with the peg key. Apart from the transaction data, the peg key
is also linked with the material-dependent master data such as the in-house source of
supplies and external procurement relationships.
When other transaction and master data is present in embedded PP/DS for a material,
deactivation and removal of the Advanced Planning indicator will result in orphaned
transactions and master data still being present in embedded PP/DS and in SAP live-
Cache. To avoid this inconsistent and orphaned data being present in embedded PP/DS,
from the SAP S/4HANA 2020 release, the removal of the Advanced Planning indicator
can’t be performed when dependent transaction data is present in embedded PP/DS. A
new field called Planning Status was also introduced to control the activation and deac-
tivation of materials for PP/DS, while the material remains integrated with PP/DS.
To uncheck the Advanced Planning indicator in the material master, follow these steps:
1. Deactivate the material for advanced planning
As shown in Figure 2.14, click on the Swap Planning Status button, which will change
the status of the material from Active for planning to Marked for deactivation. After
deactivation of the advanced planning relevancy, save the material master.

2 Master Data
58
Figure 2.14 Marking Materials for Deactivation of Advanced Planning
2. Check for the presence of dependent data
Click on the Where-Used Check button on the Advanced Planning tab in the material
master, as shown in Figure 2.15. This will execute a where-used list for this material
and search through all dependent master data and transaction data in PP/DS. If
there is dependent master and transaction data in PP/DS, you’ll see a message, as
shown in Figure 2.15, where references were found for a material in a plant. When
there are references in other master data objects found by the system, the Advanced
Planning checkbox on the screen remains noneditable. In this case, exit the material
master transaction.
3. Identify dependent data for PP/DS materials
To identify dependent objects, execute Transaction WUF (Where-Used List), and
select the Object Type 1 as Adv. Planning Location Product. The selection fields to
enter the Product Number (material number) and the Location (plant) are then dis-
played, as shown in Figure 2.16. Enter the product number and the location 2, and
click on the Execute 3 button.
In the resulting screen, you’ll see the result of the where-used analysis. Click on the
material number under the Obj. Name section 4. This will load the list of objects 5
on the right side of the screen. In the example demonstrated in Figure 2.16, only
orders are present in PP/DS for this material, so the LC Orders (SAP liveCache orders)
tab is displayed. If other objects are present in PP/DS for this material, the corre-
sponding objects such as PDSs will also be listed as tabs in the object list section.

59

Clicking on the corresponding object will display the transaction or master data
details in a table 6.

Once the dependent transaction and master data objects are identified, several
transactions and programs need to be executed to delete all such data objects. Table

5. Remove the Advanced Planning indicator
Go to the Advanced Planning tab of the material master in change mode. Click on the

sections.title: Advanced Planning Settings Specific to the Material Requirements
sections.text:
2.3.3 Advanced Planning Settings Specific to the Material Requirements
Planning Area
In the SAP S/4HANA material master, you can assign the materials to specific MRP
areas. Typically, MRP areas are created to separate the planning of specific storage loca-
tions from the plant. When MRP areas are created in the SAP S/4HANA system and
assigned to the material master, if advanced planning is activated for the material, the
system automatically activates the Advanced Planning indicator the MRP area level as
well.
Warning
When MRP areas are assigned to materials that are activated for advanced planning,
the system automatically activates the advanced planning for the material in the MRP
area as well. So, it’s mandatory to integrate the MRP areas as locations to PP/DS using
program /SAPAPO/CREATE_LOCATION before assigning advanced planning material to
the MRP areas. If the MRP area location isn’t integrated to PP/DS, an error will be raised
during the assignment of MRP areas to the materials.
As shown in Figure 2.18, navigate to the MRP 1 view 1 of the material master, and click
on the MRP Areas button 2 on the bottom of the screen. Then, navigate to the MPR area

2 Master Data
62
by double-clicking on the corresponding MRP Area 3. PP/DS-specific settings can be
maintained within the Advanced Planning tab 4 of the MRP area.
Figure 2.18 Advanced Planning View in the MRP Area
Although you can set the Advanced Planning status to Marked for deactivation in the
MRP area level, you can’t remove the Advanced Planning checkbox from the MRP area.
When the Advanced Planning checkbox is unchecked in the material master at the
plant level, the Advanced Planning flag in the MRP area is also reset.
Tip
For mass copying of PP/DS fields in the advanced planning view from the plant level to
the MRP area level, use program /SAPAPO/COPY_PLANT_TO_MRPAREA. This will only
copy the PP/DS-relevant fields available in database table MDMA.

sections.title: Flexible Integration of Material to Embedded PP/DS
sections.text:
2.3.4 Flexible Integration of Material to Embedded PP/DS
In the SAP S/4HANA material master, the concept of flexible integration is introduced
from SAP S/4HANA release 2020. This provides flexibility for how a material is inte-
grated into PP/DS by allowing you to choose the way the material is handled in PP/DS
for planning and scheduling. For example, if you want to plan the material in a plan-
ning system such as SAP Integrated Business Planning for Supply Chain (SAP IBP) and
integrate the planning results to SAP S/4HANA and to embedded PP/DS, and you want
embedded PP/DS to only perform scheduling, but not any planning, the flexible inte-
gration options can be leveraged for such requirements.
© 

63
2.3 Product Master
In the SAP S/4HANA material master under the Advanced Planning tab shown in Figure
2.19, the Scope Limitation field determines how the transaction data is integrated to PP/DS
and what actions are possible within PP/DS when such scope limitation is defined.
The Scope Profile field determines the list heuristics that are allowed to be executed in
PP/DS with specific scope limitations.
Figure 2.19 Scope Limitations in the Material Master for PP/DS Integration
The scope profile is maintained under the SAP IMG Customizing menu path SPRO 
Advanced Planning  Detailed Scheduling  Maintain Scope Profile. As shown in Figure
2.20, the default Scope Profile SAP_PPDS01 is delivered in the standard system. Select
the scope profile 1 and navigate to the Allowed Heuristics Algorithms folder to display
the list of heuristics algorithms 2 which are allowed to be executed for the materials,
when the materials are assigned with this scope profile. You can copy the SAP_PPDS01
scope profile to another profile to add or remove heuristics algorithms which are
allowed for your scope profile.
The scope limitation can only be set when activating the Advanced Planning checkbox
in the material master. Once the material is activated for advanced planning and saved,
the Scope Limitation field becomes noneditable. So, to set a scope limitation or to
change an already-set scope limitation, you must remove the Advanced Planning indi-
cator, as described earlier in Section 2.3.2, and set the advanced planning again to make
the Scope Limitation field editable.

2 Master Data
64
Figure 2.20 Scope Profile Configuration Settings
There are four scope limitation options available. A blank value in this field means
there are no limitations for integration of the transactional data from SAP S/4HANA to
PP/DS and also no restrictions on the interactive and background planning/scheduling
functions and heuristics. The details on these scope limitations are described here:
 PP/DS Display Only
With this scope limitation, all the in-house procurement orders (e.g., planned orders,
production orders, and process orders) and external procurement orders (e.g., pur-
chase requisitions, stock transfer requisitions, purchase orders, and stock transfer
orders) are integrated to PP/DS. But those will be only in display mode in PP/DS, so
they can’t be changed or deleted in PP/DS. In addition, no order creation is possible
in PP/DS for the materials with the PP/DS display only scope limitation.
No planning functions can be executed in PP/DS using any of the planning and
scheduling tools within PP/DS. In addition, no heuristics execution is possible in PP/DS
© 

65
2.3 Product Master
for planning or scheduling. This can be useful when materials planning is performed
in external systems, no scheduling is required in PP/DS, and the orders need to be
integrated to PP/DS for visibility purposes. As the execution of PP/DS heuristics isn’t
allowed for this scope limitation, the Scope Profile field isn’t relevant, and no entry
is allowed for the Scope Profile field.
 PP/DS Restricted for Inhouse Only
With this scope limitation option, external procurement orders are integrated to
PP/DS as display-only orders. These external procurement orders can’t be changed
or deleted in PP/DS, and no external procurement order creation is possible in PP/DS.
The system can only execute the heuristics that are listed under the scope profile
assigned to the material master for PP/DS interactive planning tools such as the
product view (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3) and scheduling tools such as the detailed
scheduling planning board (Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPS0), as well as in background
planning runs. The in-house procurement orders can be created, changed, and
deleted in PP/DS interactively or via automatic planning.
When there is a scope limitation that restricts the functionality within PP/DS, a
warning message is raised in interactive planning tools such as the product view
(Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3) to make you aware of the scope limitation, as shown in
Figure 2.21. In background planning runs, warning and error logs are generated if a
material can’t be planned or scheduled using a specific heuristic because it’s not part
of the scope profile configuration.
Figure 2.21 Warning on Scope Limitation in PP/DS Interactive Planning Tools
This scope limitation can be applicable in scenarios where a mix of in-house and
external procurement is possible for certain materials. The sourcing decision is

2 Master Data
66
determined in an external planning system, and you integrate the external procure-
ment orders to PP/DS. Within PP/DS, you want the system to respect the sourcing
decisions for external procurement. In addition, PP/DS needs to cover any un-covered
demand with in-house procurement orders and schedule the in-house procurement
orders with a restriction of the allowed heuristics for such materials.
 PP/DS Restricted
With this scope limitation option, you can create, change, and delete external and
in-house procurement orders in PP/DS. For heuristics execution in PP/DS, you can
only execute the heuristics that are listed in the scope profile.
This scope limitation can be leveraged in scenarios where the planning is executed
in external planning systems, but further planning functions—such as fixed peg-
ging heuristics and scheduling heuristics—are to be executed within PP/DS. In such
cases, those specific heuristics are assigned to the scope profile.
 PP/DS Entire scope for Inhouse only
This scope limitation option behaves exactly like PP/DS Restricted for In-house Only,
but there are no limitations on the list of heuristics that can be executed in PP/DS.
So, the scope profile isn’t available to be filled with this scope limitation option.
Tip
When a material is present in multiple plants, program /SAPAPO/SCOPE_LIMITATION_
LIST can be used to list the scope limitation and scope profile of the material across
plants and corresponding MRP areas.

sections.text:
2.4 Work Centers and Resources
In this section, we’ll cover resource and work center data in SAP S/4HANA and how that
data is integrated into PP/DS. We’ll also discuss the specifics of PP/DS resource master data.
Resources and work centers represent the machines, tools, and labor resources that are
used to manufacture products. In industries that follow continuous or process manu-
facturing (e.g., the chemical industry), the term resource is used to represent the pro-
duction resources; in discrete manufacturing scenarios, the production resources are
called work centers.
Work centers and resources hold basic information about their usage in the production
process, capacity definition, and scheduling data. In SAP S/4HANA, the data related to the
activity types, which are used to derive the cost of the resource usage, plays a crucial role.
In embedded PP/DS, the resource master data maintenance is simplified by eliminat-
ing the need to create an integration model for transferring the work centers and
resources to PP/DS.
© 

67
2.4 Work Centers and Resources

sections.title: Work Centers
sections.text:
2.4.1 Work Centers
Work centers are created in SAP S/4HANA by executing Transaction CR01 and are
changed by executing Transaction CR02. After you execute Transaction CR01, enter a
Plant, Work Center name, and Category, and then press (Enter) to arrive at the screen
shown in Figure 2.22. In the Basic Data tab of the work center master data, select the
Advanced Planning indicator.
Figure 2.22 Activation of Advanced Planning in the SAP S/4HANA Work Center
After the Advanced Planning indicator is selected, the resource is transferred to embed-
ded PP/DS. In embedded PP/DS, the following four resource types are supported:
 Single activity resource
Only one activity can be performed in this resource at a given time. The available
capacity is defined only as a dimension of time.
 Multi-activity resource
Multiple activities can be performed in this resource in parallel. The available capac-
ity is defined as the time dimension, along with the number of individual capacities
available.

2 Master Data
68
 Production line
Line resources are typically used in rate-based manufacturing such as automotive
assembly lines.
 Calendar resources
These resources don’t hold any capacity, but they are used for determining the sched-
ule of the activity performed in these resources. The handling resources that are
assigned to the location master data to schedule the GR/GI processing times
(inbound and outbound handling resources) are created as calendar resources.
Although there is no need to schedule these handling activities based on any capaci-
ties, a resource is still required in PP/DS to determine the schedule of those activities.
The PP/DS properties (e.g., resource type, category, validity of the resource time
streams, etc.) are defaulted from the customizing maintained in Transaction CFC9
under the Initial Data Transfer and Change Transfer for Resource section, as shown in
Figure 2.23.
Figure 2.23 Default Values for PP/DS Resource Transfer
The default values for the PP/DS resource properties, such as the resource type, cate-
gory, and validity of the resource time stream, can be overwritten in the work center
master data in SAP S/4HANA. You can use the APO Resource button in the capacity
header of the work center master data from Transaction CR01 or Transaction CR02 to
define the work center–specific PP/DS resource properties, as shown in Figure 2.24.
Resource Cat. (resource category) is a descriptive field for denoting the usage of the
resource and doesn’t have a functional significance for scheduling. The time stream
validity is determined by the fields Days - (days in past) and Days + (days in future), and
the same is used to create the SAP liveCache time stream in PP/DS.
© 

69
2.4 Work Centers and Resources
Figure 2.24 PP/DS Resource Properties in the SAP S/4HANA Work Center
Note
In the SAP S/4HANA work center, you’ll still see fields and resource types relevant to
the standalone PP/DS component of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization sce-
nario. In a side-by-side SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization and SAP S/4HANA
system, these resource types are still relevant, so they are still present but not relevant
for embedded PP/DS.
In the PPO Capacity Constraints tab, the relevant parameters for the Production Plan-
ning Optimizer are maintained. The Production Planning Optimizer was introduced in
SAP S/4HANA 2020 release and aids in achieving an optimal production plan. We’ll
cover the details and functionality of the Production Planning Optimizer in Chapter 5,
Section 5.8.
After the work center is transferred to embedded PP/DS by setting the Advanced Plan-
ning checkbox, the resource is available for maintenance of additional data in the PP/DS
transaction. Execute Transaction /SAPAPO/RES01 to access the PP/DS resource master
data. You can also follow SAP menu path, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Master Data 
Resource  Resource, to access the resource master.
Because the resources are created in PP/DS, they are assigned to planning version 000.
There is also a version-independent resource that is created in PP/DS. Certain pieces
of PP/DS resource data, such as the classification of resources for characteristics-
dependent planning (CDP), are maintained in the version-independent resource data.

2 Master Data
70
As shown in Figure 2.25, you can enter the Resource and the Location in the initial
screen. In the Model and Plng Version section, enter the Planning Version “000” for the
active version of the resource, or check the Model-Independent Selection checkbox to
access the model-independent version of the resource. Click the Change Resources but-
ton or the Display Resources button to change or display the resource details, respec-
tively.
Figure 2.25 Resource Master in PP/DS in SAP S/4HANA: Initial Screen
Tip
When the work centers are transferred to embedded PP/DS, the work center name is
prefixed with the letter “W”, and the suffix of the location and the capacity category is
added. For example, work center S4PPDS_W created in plant 0001 with capacity cate-
gory 001 is created as WS4PPDS_W_0001_001 in PP/DS.
In the details of the PP/DS resource, the resource and basic information is displayed in
list form, when the Model-Independent Selection checkbox is set and the Planning Ver-
sion is also set in the selection screen shown in Figure 2.25, the resource master data in
version 000 and also the version-independent resource master are listed (see Figure
2.26 1) and the details are available in the individual tabs 2. Under the PP/DS Bucket
Cap. tab, there is an option to set the PP/DS bucket capacity, which is used for planning
capacity at a daily or shift-wise buckets, but that isn’t valid for embedded PP/DS. The
only bucket capacity supported in SAP S/4HANA is the block planning scenario bucket,
which is set when the resource is enabled for block planning. We’ll cover more details
about block planning in Chapter 8, Section 8.3.2, when discussing advanced PP/DS fea-
tures.
© 

71
2.4 Work Centers and Resources
Figure 2.26 PP/DS Resource Master Data: Details
In the ExternalCap. tab, you can view the source of the capacity definition. If the External
Capacity checkbox is selected, the capacity defined in the SAP S/4HANA work center is
considered for the capacity definition. If the capacity definition needs to be maintained
in embedded PP/DS, the External Capacity checkbox should not be selected.
The downtimes or nonworking times due to planned or repair maintenance of the
resources can be directly maintained in the Downtimes tab of the resource master. In
addition, when an SAP S/4HANA plant maintenance order can be integrated into PP/DS
and a work center is assigned to the maintenance order, the maintenance duration is
entered automatically as downtime in the PP/DS resource master.
Specific fields such as the Setup Matrix shown in Figure 2.26 can be changed in the
PP/DS resource master. Other settings for the resource are only maintained in the
SAP S/4HANA work center under the APO Resource view under the capacity header,
as shown earlier in Figure 2.24.
Warning
Clicking on the overview/details or (Ctrl)+(F8) in the resource displays the resource
details in an overview list that enables you to change values for fields that aren’t edit-
able in the detailed screen of the PP/DS resource master. Changing values here can cre-
ate conflicts with the SAP S/4HANA work center master data, so don’t change any
values in the overview option for fields available in the SAP S/4HANA work center APO
Resource view.

2 Master Data
72

sections.title: Resources
sections.text:
2.4.2 Resources
In production planning for process industries in SAP S/4HANA (in SAP ERP, known as
PP-PI) with process industry scenarios where continuous flow, processing, and storage
vessels are required to be modeled in the master data, resources are created instead of
work centers. One of the main differences between the resources and work centers is
the category of the work center or the resource. In work center creation, you have the
options to assign categories such as Machine, Labor, or Production Line. In resources,
you have categories such as Processing Unit, Storage Resources, and the combination
of both, depending on the resource category.
In this section, we’ll see examples of the Processing Unit and Storage Resource categories.
Resources are created in the SAP S/4HANA system using Transaction CRC1 or via the SAP
Easy Access menu path, Logistics  Production – Process  Master Data  Resources 
Resource  Create.
In the initial screen for resource creation, enter the Plant and a name for the Resource.
Select the Resource category as 0015 – Proc. unit/Stor . res., as shown in Figure 2.27.
Figure 2.27 Resource Creation in Production Planning for Process Industries: Initial Screen
In the next screen, fill in all required fields such as the Person Responsible and the
Usage. The Stor. Loc. Res., which represents the storage location, is assigned to the
resource, as shown in Figure 2.28. For resources that can store materials, the inventory
available in this assigned storage location is leveraged by PP/DS in the tank planning
functionality. We’ll cover the details of tank planning in Chapter 8, Section 8.5.
© 

73
2.4 Work Centers and Resources
For making the resource available in PP/DS, activate the Advanced Planning checkbox.
Figure 2.28 Resource Creation in SAP S/4HANA
Navigate to the Capacities tab, and click on the Capacity header. In the capacity header,
click on the APO Resource button. As shown in Figure 2.29, navigate to the Storage
Characteristics tab to enter the PP/DS storage properties of the resource.
Activation of the Storage Characteristics checkbox defines the resource as a resource
with storage capacity apart from the production capacity. For example, the production
capacity indicates that the resource has an availability of 24 hours, and the storage
capacity indicates that the resource can also store a maximum of 10,000 gallons of liq-
uids.
As shown in Figure 2.29, enter the Storage Dimension, which is typically mass or vol-
ume. Also enter a unit of measurement for the storage capacity (Stock Unit), along with
the Min Production Qty (minimum production quantity, which must be filled for the

2 Master Data
74
storage resource) and the Maximum Stock Level of the storage resource. The Set
Remaining Fill Level to Zero checkbox helps in ensuring product purity of the materials
stored in the storage resource. For example, if Liquid 1 is to be filled in the storage
resource, and that resource has Liquid 2 in storage already, with this flag set, the system
sets the resource’s fill level to 0 and raises an alert in PP/DS to inform the scheduler
that the resource contains another product. But if there is a small remaining quantity
of the product in the storage resource that is under a certain value, the system is
allowed to set the resource’s fill level to 0, and this value is maintained in the Threshold
(Set Zero) field. When the Allow Multiple Products checkbox is switched on, the system
allows multiple materials to be stored in the storage container at the same time. There-
fore, this flag and Set Remaining Fill Level to Zero are mutually exclusive.
Figure 2.29 Maintenance of Storage Characteristics in the Resource Master Data in SAP
S/4HANA
In the table under Time-Dependent Storage Data, Min. Production Qty, Maximum Stock
Level, and Threshold (Set Zero) can be maintained in a time-phased manner. For exam-
ple, if the maximum storage can be 10,000 gallons in the colder months, and the max-
imum storage can only be 8,000 gallons in the warmer months, it can be achieved by
the time-dependent storage data settings shown in Figure 2.29.
Resources that aren’t storage relevant are created with the Processing Unit resource
category, and only the capacity details are maintained in the capacity header of the
resource master in the SAP S/4HANA system.
© 

75

sections.title: Sources of Supply
sections.text:
2.5 Sources of Supply
2.5 Sources of Supply
In this section, we’ll cover the various sources of supply supported in the SAP S/4HANA
system and how these can be transferred to PP/DS for their usage in planning.
The sources of supply in embedded PP/DS refers to how the material will be produced or
procured. For in-house production of products, the sources of supply in SAP S/4HANA
include bills of material (BOMs), routings, and production versions, which combine the
BOM and routing for a specific product. In addition, for the process industries, the mas-
ter recipe is the in-house source of supply that comprises the manufacturing steps in
the form of operations and phases in production and the BOM.
Materials that are procured externally from suppliers and materials transferred
between plants, which are the external procurement sources of supplies in ERP sys-
tems, include purchase info records, scheduling agreements, and contracts.

sections.title: Production Data Structure
sections.text:
2.5.1 Production Data Structure
For the in-house sources of supply in embedded PP/DS, the source of supply is called a
production data structure (PDS), which contains all the basic, material, and scheduling
information as defined in SAP S/4HANA BOMs, routings, and production versions. As
shown in Figure 2.30, the validity of dates, lot sizes for which this production version
can be used, and the BOM and routing information are maintained in the production
version master data.
Figure 2.30 Production Version Master Data in SAP S/4HANA

sections.title: Transfer of Routing to PP/DS as Production Data Structures
sections.text:
2.5.2 Transfer of Routing to PP/DS as Production Data Structures
Execute Transaction CURTOADV_CREATE to create the PDSs in embedded PP/DS by
processing SAP S/4HANA master data. You can also navigate to SAP menu path, Logis-
tics  Production  Master Data  PDS for Advanced Planning  PDS Transfer (PP/DS), to
execute the transfer.

2 Master Data
76
The material for which the PDS is being transferred must be flagged for advanced plan-
ning. If multiple material components are part of the BOM, only the material compo-
nents flagged for advanced planning will be created as the components in the PDS data
in embedded PP/DS.
Similarly, the operations to which the work centers are assigned to the routing opera-
tions must be flagged for advanced planning. Standard value key—the scheduling and
capacity requirements formula—should be maintained in the work center data. The
routing operation must also have a nonzero activity time calculated during the sched-
uling, and the control key assigned to the operation should allow scheduling.
Note
In SAP S/4HANA, it’s mandatory to have production versions for the consideration of
BOMs and routings in the MRP run and source of supply determination. You can use
report CS_BOM_PRODVER_MIGRATION02 to create production versions in an auto-
mated manner.
The selection screen of the PDS transfer is shown in Figure 2.31. The PDS must be avail-
able in the PP/DS active version, so enter the value “000” for Pl. Version in APO, and
then enter the selection options for which you need to transfer the PDS to embedded
PP/DS under Selection Criteria.
PDSs are also used to manage the component requirements in the subcontracting sce-
narios, where a product is manufactured completely or partly by a third-party vendor,
and the plant sends the components to the vendor to complete the manufacturing pro-
cess. In these cases, a production version for manufacturing is linked to the purchase
info records or scheduling agreements, and the corresponding PDSs also can be created
in embedded PP/DS. You can define the relevance of the PDS for the subcontracting
scenario in the PDS Type section of the selection screen.
You can see more options for the PDS transfer by scrolling down the screen, as shown
in Figure 2.32. You can use the Extended Consistency Check checkbox to ensure the con-
sistency of the PDS data in embedded PP/DS. Because this performance-intensive
option does a lot of checks and validations, don’t use the Extended Consistency Check
setting for transferring the PDS data periodically.
© 

77
2.5 Sources of Supply
Figure 2.31 PDS Transfer to PP/DS: Selection Screen
Figure 2.32 PP/DS in SAP S/4HANA: PDS Transfer Options
When errors are generated in embedded PP/DS during the PDS transfer, the changes in
master data aren’t transferred from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS. However, the
PDS will continue to be used in the PP/DS planning. If you want to avoid this situation,
select the Lock PDS in error case checkbox in the options. This will lock the PDS and
avoid its usage in planning until the PDS integration is successfully completed.

2 Master Data
78
Checking the Absolute Transfer checkbox to perform a complete transfer of the PDS
data to PP/DS will regenerate the PDS based on the date from SAP S/4HANA. Conversely,
the Change Transfer option is used for sending the changes made to SAP S/4HANA mas-
ter data, such as BOMs, routings, and production versions, after the PDS is transferred
to PP/DS.
The transfer mode Absolute Transfer (Delta Mode) will create PDSs in PP/DS for newly
created production versions in SAP S/4HANA, for example, if there are 10 PDSs that are
already created in a plant for existing production versions and 3 new production ver-
sions created in the SAP S/4HANA system. When executing the PDS creation via Trans-
action CURTOADV_CREATE, with Plant as the only selection option and with the
transfer mode Absolute Transfer (Delta Mode), this will only create the three new PDSs.
With the transfer mode Absolute Transfer, it will send all 13 production versions to PP/DS
for PDS generation.
Tip
Use Transaction CURTOADV_CRT_FOCUS for creating PDSs corresponding to order or
work breakdown structure (WBS) BOMs in SAP S/4HANA. Because the WBS and order
BOMs are specific to the sales order documents and WBS elements in the project sys-
tem, a separate transaction is provided for selecting the order and WBS BOMs.
The PDS transfer can be executed in interactive mode using Transaction /SAPAPO/
CURTOADV_CREATE or can be scheduled as a background job with a selection variant
defined for this transaction. The transfer logs are displayed immediately in the interac-
tive mode, and the transfer log can be viewed from the application logs in background
mode via Transaction SLG1 by entering “CIF” in the Object field.
In embedded PP/DS, Transaction /SAPAPO/CURTO_SIMU is used to select and display
the PDS data. As shown in Figure 2.33, after executing the transaction, you enter the
Product Number, Location, and Planning Version in the selection screen to filter the PDS
selection. Additional selections are also possible by providing an Order Number in
embedded PP/DS where the PDS is used.
In addition, for the PDSs that have a specific account assignment, such as a sales order,
the Special Stock and Account Assignment Element fields can be used for selection with
the sales document number. These sales documents should be transferred before the
PDSs are generated with reference to them. Click the Execute button to display the list
of PDSs selected per the selection criteria provided.
In the next screen, the list of PDSs is displayed, as shown in Figure 2.34. To view the
details, double-click on the corresponding PDS in the list. In the list view on the first
section of the screen, the basic details from the SAP S/4HANA production version are
displayed. The validity dates and lot sizes are copied from the production version data.
© 

79
2.5 Sources of Supply
Figure 2.33 PP/DS PDS Selection Screen
Figure 2.34 PDS Display in PP/DS

2 Master Data
80
The PDS details are shown in multiple sections and tabs, as shown in Figure 2.34:
 Components
All the material components that are transferred from the BOM linked to the pro-
duction version are shown here. The header of the BOM is listed as an output com-
ponent, and the components of the BOM are listed as input components.
 Operations
The operations that are relevant to PP/DS are transferred to this tab of the PDS. For
master recipes, the operations and the phases under the operations are also listed
here.
 Activities
One operation can contain multiple activities, such as the setup, production, and
tear-down activities. The activities for all the operations are listed in this tab. The lot
size dependency of the operation and also the base quantity defined in the opera-
tion in the routing are transferred to the individual activities in the PDS. The dura-
tion of the activities is calculated by the standard values for the activities defined in
the routing operations.
 Activity Relatshps
The activities belonging to different operations form relationships in the PDS based
on the relationships defined in the routing operations. For example, activities fol-
lowing a sequence will have an end-start relationship. The relationships of all the
operations activities are listed in this tab.
 Sequence Groups
When parallel sequences are maintained in the routing, the sequence group infor-
mation is listed in the Sequence Groups tab.
The created modes are shown under the activities. The mode is the object in the PDS
that holds the actual duration of the activity. As shown in Figure 2.35, the setup, prod-
uct and teardown activities have their own modes, and the duration of the modes are
calculated according to the SAP S/4HANA work center formula and the standard values
maintained in the SAP S/4HANA routing. The calculated value in the routings can be
checked by executing the scheduling in the routing. During the PDS transfer to PP/DS,
similar calculations are performed to determine the mode durations in the PDS. The
mode durations are calculated with seconds as the unit of measure for the time. For
checking the scheduling result of the routing in Transaction CA03, in the menu bar,
select Extras  Scheduling  Schedule.
The mapping of the operation durations based on the routing scheduling and the cor-
responding values in the PDS modes is shown in Figure 2.35. For example, the 10 min
duration 1 for the produce activity (displayed as Edit in Figure 2.35 2) of the operation
0010 3 is shown as 600 seconds of mode duration 4 in the PDS under the Produce
activity 5.
© 

81
2.5 Sources of Supply
Figure 2.35 Mapping of Mode Durations in PP/DS PDS from SAP S/4HANA Routings
Tip
When work centers in SAP S/4HANA are assigned with a class of type 019 with the
same characteristics value, and if the routing operation is also assigned with the same
class and the same characteristics value, during the PDS transfer all such work centers
are created as alternative modes under the activity. For example, work centers WC1,
WC2, and WC3 have class C1 and characteristics CHR1 with value of V1, and the routing
operation is also assigned with Class CI with value V1 for the CHR1 characteristics. In
this case, the PDS in PP/DS will have three alternative modes with WC1, WC2, and WC3
as possible resources under the activities generated from the routing operation.
In embedded PP/DS, the PDS is only available for display, meaning the information
can’t be changed. For the data that originates from the SAP S/4HANA master data (e.g.,
BOM, routing, and production version), the source of truth is the SAP S/4HANA master
data, which can’t be changed in the PDS.
However, some of the PP/DS PDS data can be maintained in Transaction PDS_MAINT in
SAP S/4HANA. Procurement priority of the PDS for the source of supply selection
during the planning run or the costs associated with the individual PDSs can be main-
tained in Transaction PDS_MAINT. After such PP/DS PDS data is maintained via the
maintenance transaction, the PDS needs to be retransferred to embedded PP/DS using
Transaction CURTOADV_CREATE to reflect the changes there.

2 Master Data
82
Tip
When PDSs are copied into inactive planning versions (000 is the active planning ver-
sion to which the PDS is integrated from SAP S/4HANA), Transaction /SAPAPO/CURTO_
EDIT can be used to edit the PDS.

sections.title: Transfer of Master Recipes as Production Data Structures to PP/DS
sections.text:
2.5.3 Transfer of Master Recipes as Production Data Structures to PP/DS
When production planning for process industries recipes is used in the SAP S/4HANA
system for process manufacturing scenarios, the overall process of transferring the
production version from SAP S/4HANA to a PDS in PP/DS remains similar to the trans-
fer of routings to PP/DS as PDSs. But for the determination of the activities under the
operations, a different method is used.
The structure of the production planning for process industries master recipe is shown
in Figure 2.36. Master recipes are created in the SAP S/4HANA system using Transaction
C201. Unlike the routings, in master recipes, the operations have phases under them.
For example, in a scenario where a chemical reaction operation of a manufacturing
process is involved, and that operation requires 30 min of setup time to clean the reac-
tor vessel and 1 hour of reaction time per 100 KG of materials, the recipe will have an
operation 1 for Chemical Reaction under which phases 2 will be created. The first
phase is for the clean-up/setup time, and the second phase is created for the actual
chemical reaction process.
Figure 2.36 Structure of a Master Recipe in SAP S/4HANA
For the PDS transfer to PP/DS, the setup phase will be identified by the assignment of a
setup group to the phase of the master recipe. Phases with a setup group will become
setup activities under the operation in the PDS, and other phases will be transferred as
product activities. Apart from the setup group assignment to the phase in the master
© 

83
2.5 Sources of Supply
recipe, it’s also required to have a finish-start (FS) relationship between the setup and
produce phases in the master recipe. The setup group needs to be integrated to PP/DS
before the transfer of the PDS. Maintenance and integration of setup groups will be
covered in Section 2.8. In the example shown in Figure 2.37, phase 0020 is assigned with
a setup group 1 and has a FS relationship 2 with the phase 0030. The mapping of this
phase as a setup activity in the PDS is also shown in Figure 2.37. The phase with the
setup group assigned is created as a setup activity 3, and the duration of the setup
activity is set as 30 min (1,800 sec 4).
Figure 2.37 Mapping of the Setup Phase to the Setup Activity between Master Recipe and PDS

sections.title: External Procurement Sources of Supply
sections.text:
2.5.4 External Procurement Sources of Supply
In SAP S/4HANA, the sources of supply for external procurement include the following:
 Purchase info records
Purchase info records in the SAP S/4HANA system represent the purchasing relation-
ship of a material with its supplier. The purchase info record contains the informa-
tion-specific procurement lead times, quantity restrictions, and pricing conditions,
which are valid for the material and the vendor. The info records are defined at the
purchasing organization level and can also have plant-level information. In addition,
the info records can be classified as standard info records or subcontracting info
records, among other types.

2 Master Data
84
 Scheduling agreements
Scheduling agreements are documents created at the plant level for procurement of
material vendors on an agreed schedule. After the scheduling agreement is in place,
the schedule line releases can be manually created, or the system can create sched-
ule line releases via planning runs.
 Contracts
Contracts or outline agreements are documents created with a negotiated value or
quantity of a material and follow-on purchasing documents such as purchase orders
or schedule lines created to initiate the procurement.
In embedded PP/DS, the purchase info records, contracts, and scheduling agreements
are supported as external procurement relationships, which can be used by PP/DS

2.6 Classes and Characteristics
In this section, we’ll discuss the usage of classes and characteristics in embedded PP/DS
as well as how the classes and characteristics are maintained in the system. A character-
istic denotes a specific attribute of a product, such as color, capacity, usage, and so on.
Characteristics that define a set of attributes of a product are grouped under a class.
In PP/DS planning, there are two ways to use the classification system:
 Characteristics-dependent planning (CDP)
CDP is used in in-house manufacturing processes to match the characteristics of the
demand element, such as sales order or dependent demand, to a supply element
that has the same characteristics value assignment (also called characteristics valua-
tion). The CDP scenario supports both make-to-stock (MTS) and make-to-order
(MTO) planning scenarios.
 Variant configuration (VC)
VC is used for complex configurable products mainly in MTO scenarios where the
specification of the product in the sales order drives the manufacturing processes.
Either in CDP or VC scenarios, the classes and characteristics play the major role in
transferring the configuration of the product from the demand level to the manufac-
turing level. Class types are defined in the SAP S/4HANA system to allow them to be
© 

89

used in a specific scenario. We’ll cover the configuration schema (CDP versus VC) of the
PP/DS system in Chapter 3 when we discuss configuration.

data, as shown in Figure 2.44.

2.7 Quota Arrangements
Quota arrangements are used to allocate the demand quantities to multiple receipts
using different sources of supplies in a predefined ratio. This can be for both in-house
manufacturing sources of supplies for in-house manufacturing and external procure-
ment sources of supply for external procurement.
When multiple sources of supplies are available, the quota arrangement master data is
used to determine what portion of the demand is fulfilled by which source. For the in-
© 

93
2.7 Quota Arrangements
house production scenario, the quota can allocate the demand quantities between
available PDSs. For example, if there are two manufacturing lines represented by two
different PDSs in PP/DS, and if you want to allocate 70% of the demand to line 1 and
30% of the demand to line 2, this can be achieved by setting up the quota arrangement
master data. Similarly for external procurement, where there are multiple vendors sup-
plying the same material and you want to split the demand between these available
vendors in a certain percentage allocation, quota arrangement can help. In addition, if
there are stock transfer scenarios, such as two plants that can supply the material to
one plant, and you want to allocate the demand to the supplying plants in certain per-
centages, the quota arrangement can be leveraged by assigning the percentage alloca-
tion between the transportation lanes of these locations.
In the embedded PP/DS system, the quota arrangement master data is created using
Transaction /SAPAPO/SCC_TQ1 or the SAP Easy Access menu path, Logistics  Advanced
Planning  Master Data  Quota Arrangement  Quota Arrangement.

sections.title: Setup Matrix
sections.text:
2.8 Setup Matrix
Setup matrix master data is the definition of the changeover duration and cost
between different operations executed on the same resource. The changeover duration
and cost are typically based on the characteristics of the product being produced in the
relevant operation. In this section, we’ll cover the details of the static setup matrix and
the PP/DS generated setup matrix, which are based on the characteristics assigned to
the products.
In embedded PP/DS, the setup matrix is used to determine the changeover time
between two operations on a resource. For example, if black paint and white paint are
being packaged on the same packing line, and after a production order is executed for
packing black paint, the packaging line needs a thorough cleaning before the white
paint order is started. If this cleaning process takes 30 minutes (min), the changeover
time from the black paint order to white paint order is 30 min.
There can also be more complex changeover situations. In the preceding example,
apart from the color transition, if there are multiple sizes of packed products being
packed, for example, 50 grams (g), 100 g, and 500 g packaging, and they have their own
changeover time to unload and reload the packaging materials to the lines, it makes the
possible combinations of transitions complex. The changeover of 50 g black to 100 g
black may just take 5 min because only the packaging material needs to be changed,
whereas the changeover from 50 g black to 100 g white will take 30 min for cleaning
and 5 min for loading the new packaging material. In addition, if the cleaning and the
loading of packaging material is performed in parallel, the changeover will be 30 mins,
but if these tasks are done sequentially, the changeover will be 35 min (30 min for
cleaning and 5 min for loading). These possible combinations for changeovers are typ-
ically maintained in a matrix.
To address such simple and complex transitions in the embedded PP/DS solution,
there are two setup matrix options provided:
 Conventional setup matrix (static setup groups)
 Generated setup matrix (dynamic setup groups)
© 

97
2.8 Setup Matrix

sections.text:
2.8.1 Static Setup Matrix
In the static setup matrix, the setup groups are the conditions for the changeovers. For
example, all black paint products are in setup group Black, and all white paint products
are in setup group White. These groups are assigned in the corresponding operation
within the routing. If there are some exceptions within the group, for example, if the
packet size needs to be transitioned from 50 g to 500 g, which takes an additional 15
min of changeover time, setup keys with the setup groups can help with that.
The setup groups and setup keys are created in the SAP S/4HANA system and assigned
to the routing operations. The setup groups and setup keys need to be transferred to
the embedded PP/DS system via an integration model. Then, the transfer of routing
from SAP S/4HANA to the embedded PP/DS PDS will assign the corresponding setup
groups to the PDS operations and activities.
To create the setup groups and keys in the SAP S/4HANA system, follow the IMG menu
path, SPRO  Production  Capacity Requirements  Planning  Master Data  Routing Data 
Define Setup Parameters. Within this Customizing node, click on the Setup group cate-
gory option.
Click on the New Entries button. As shown in Figure 2.52 ,enter the setup group names,
and press (Enter). Select the setup group name, and double-click on the Setup group
key. Click on the New Entries button, and enter the setup key values. Similarly, enter
the setup group and keys for all required transition scenarios.

the integration model via Transaction CFM2. This will make the setup group and keys
available in PP/DS.

The setup keys should have different names from the setup groups, and the same
setup key name can’t be used across multiple setup groups. Violating this will cause
core interface queue failures during the integration model activation.
Assign the setup groups and keys in the routing operation, as shown in Figure 2.53.
Double-click on the operation 1, and scroll down to find the setup group and setup key
fields 2. the transfer of the corresponding production version to embedded PP/DS will

2.8.2 Generated Setup Matrix
When a complex changeover is needed due to the combination of characteristics of the
products being manufactured on the same production lines, generating setup groups
and setup keys for all the possible transition combinations would be a tedious task. For
example, in the food industry, the characteristics of a product include kosher versus
nonkosher products, products containing allergens versus nonallergen-containing
products, different flavors of the food being produced, or different packaging sizes. Cre-
ating setup groups and keys for the preceding mentioned possible combinations (e.g.,
changeover from kosher-allergen-savory 10 oz pack to kosher-nonallergen-savory 10
oz pack takes 30 min of changeover time) and assigning them in the master recipe
phases would be almost an impossible task.
© 

101
2.8 Setup Matrix
To handle such requirements in embedded PP/DS, you can use the generated setup
matrix. The generated setup matrix works based on the classification of the product
itself, and the system generates the combinations for the changeovers. There is no
need to assign the setup groups to the routings or master recipe operations, as the sys-
tem reads the classification data of the material to determine the setup group dynami-
cally and derives the changeover (setup) times from the setup matrix.

two characteristics: color and pack size. COLOR has the characteristics values of BLACK,

ues maintained in the characteristics master data) or Generation via BAdI (in this
case, you can implement your own custom ABAP coding logic for the generation of
setup groups).
Figure 2.59 Setup Group Rule Generation in PP/DS

2.8 Setup Matrix
In the Prefix field, you can maintain any characters that should be prefixed to the
generated setup groups (e.g., CP – color pack size, will generate the setup group
names starting with the characters “CP”). In the Separator field, you can maintain a
character to serve as the separator (e.g., -); in this case, the setup group will be created
as characteristic value X “-” characteristic value Y (BLACK-500).
You also can maintain the characteristics 4 on which you want the setup groups to
be generated. In our example, we’ll assign two characteristics: S4PPDSCOLOR and
S4PPDSPCKSIZE 5. You can assign up to six characteristics for the setup group gen-
eration.
4. Maintain rules for generating setup matrices
Now that we’ve created the characteristics value matrix and the rule for generating
the setup groups, we’ll define the rules for generation of the setup matrix. To create
the setup group generation rules, you can use Transaction /SAPAPO/MATRULE or
the SAP Easy Access menu path, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Master Data  Setup
Group/Setup Matrix  Generate Setup Matrices  Maintain Rules for Generating
Setup Matrices.
In the initial screen of the transaction, enter the location in which you want to gen-
erate the rule for the generation of the setup matrix (rule). In the next screen, you’ll
see the list of existing rules; to create a new rule, click on the New Entry button.
As shown in Figure 2.60 , enter the Location in which the rule is generated, enter a
name in the Setup Matrix field for the setup matrix on which this rule will be applied
(here, S4PPDSCOLOR_PCK). Under Settings 1, enter the setup group rule (SetupGrp
Rule), which we’ve created in the preceding step (S4PPDSGENRULE1). The Type of For-
mula field determines how the setup times are determined: the Determine Cost and
Duration Using Formula value derives the setup duration from the characteristics
value matrix, where we’ve defined the changeover (setup) duration; the Determine
Duration and Costs Using BAdI allows you to define your custom ABAP-based logic
by implementing the logic in the BAdI (/SAPAPO/CDPS_MATGEN) enhancement.
The Formula: Durat. (formula for duration calculation) field has two values: The
Total value will add up all the times for the individual characteristics value transi-
tion (e.g., if black to white transition is 60 mins, and transition from 100 g to 50 g is
10 mins, then the setup time between Black 100 g to White 50 g will be calculated as
70 mins). The Maximum value considers the maximum among the setup times
between the possible changeover times and then sets the maximum of that as the
setup time for the transition of the combination (e.g., if black to white transition is
60 mins, and transition from 100 g to 50 g is 10 mins, then the setup time between
Black 100 g to White 50 g will be calculated as 60 mins, which is the maximum com-
paring 60 mins and 10 mins).
Under the Characteristics Value Matrices 2 section, enter the characteristics value
matrices that must be part of the generated setup matrix.

Figure 2.60 Maintenance of Setup Matrix Generation Rule
5. Generate and display the setup matrix
The next step is the generation of the setup matrix for all the possible characteristics
value combinations based on the rule for the setup groups generation and the rule
for the setup matrix generation. To generate the setup matrix, use Transaction
/SAPAPO/CDPS_MATGEN or the SAP Easy Access menu path, Logistics  Advanced
Planning  Master Data  Setup Group/Setup Matrix  Generate Setup Matrices  Gen-
erate Setup Matrices.
In this transaction, as shown in Figure 2.61 1, you can enter the Location and the
Setup Matrix name (in our example, PPS2 and S4PPDSCOLOR_PCK, respectively,
which we maintained in the preceding step). The Flagged Setup Matrices checkbox
will generate (for a new matrix) or regenerate (for an existing setup matrix) if there
are any changes made to the characteristic value matrix or in the generation rules.
Clicking on the execute button will generate the setup matrix. If the generation is
successful, you’ll see a success message 2.
The generated setup matrix can be displayed from Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPS_
SETUP or under the SAP Easy Access menu path, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Mas-
ter Data  Setup Group/Setup Matrix  Display Setup Matrix. In the initial screen of
this transaction 3, enter the Location and the Setup Matrix name, and execute the
transaction. The generated setup matrix based on the characteristics value matrix
and the rules is displayed in the next screen 4.

6. Assign the setup matrix to the PP/DS resource
In this step, we’ll assign the setup matrix to the resource master data in PP/DS. As
shown in Figure 2.62, in the resource master data Transaction /SAPAPO/RES01, nav-
igate to the Time-Cont. Capacity tab. In the Setup Matrix field, enter the setup
matrix, which is applicable for the changeover duration calculation for the orders/
operations executed on the resource.

With SAP S/4HANA routings, when there is a setup time maintained in the routing
operation (see Figure 2.63 1), and a corresponding setup formula is maintained in the
work center master data 2, the generated PDS in PP/DS will have a setup activity. The
setup activity in the PDS is identified with the activity type (Act. Type) 3. If the resource
corresponding to the SAP S/4HANA work center is assigned with the generated setup
matrix, in the PDS, the setup activity and all the other activities belonging to the same
operation will have the indicator Setup group from the characteristics value assign-

Figure 2.63 Setup Activity with Generated Setup Matrix and SAP S/4HANA Routings
When master recipes are used in the SAP S/4HANA system, as shown in Figure 2.64,
there should be a dedicated setup phase 1 created under the operation 2. In addition,
when a setup activity is present in the PDS, it must be followed by a produce activity in
the PDS. This produce activity is represented by another phase 3 in the master recipe
operation. The setup phase and the produce phase should have a relationship 4 defined
in the master recipe. In this example, the 0020-setup phase and the 0030-produce phase
are related with a FS (finish start relationship) 5. When the resource in PP/DS is
assigned with a setup matrix and in the recipe under the operation using the same
resource, the first phase will be transferred to the PP/DS PDS as a setup activity, as
shown in Figure 2.64. The setup activity in the PDS is identified with the activity type
(Act. Type) 6. If the resource corresponding to the SAP S/4HANA work center is
assigned with the generated setup matrix, in the PDS, the setup activity and all the
other activities belonging to the same operation will have the Setup Grp 7 indicator set

2.9 Summary
Figure 2.64 Setup Activity with Generated Setup Matrix in the SAP S/4HANA Master Recipe
When an operation of an order is placed on a resource, the system will evaluate if there
is a setup matrix assigned to the resource. If that is a generated setup matrix, the sys-
tem evaluates the classification (class/characteristics values) of the product and deter-
mines the setup group dynamically. When an operation of an order is followed by
another order, the system derives the changeover (setup) time based on the data gen-
erated by the setup matrix.
2.9 Summary
In this chapter, we covered the basic and most commonly used master data objects in
embedded PP/DS. In addition, we covered the various methods to integrate the differ-

2 Master Data
110
ent master data objects from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS and also the details on
master data objects, which are maintained within embedded PP/DS.
The material master and resource masters are transferred by simply activating the
Advanced Planning checkbox in the master data in SAP S/4HANA. For locations and
PDSs, the ABAP programs are executed to initiate the transfer of the data to embedded
PP/DS. For external procurement, integration models need to be created and activated
to transfer the master data for source supplies, such as purchase info records, schedul-
ing agreements, and contracts, as well as classes used in the CDP scenario. For setup
groups, such as the static setup groups, the setup groups/keys are integrated via inte-
gration model. The setup matrix is created and maintained within embedded PP/DS
for both static and dynamic setup matrices.
We’ll cover other PP/DS master data objects, such as time-dependent safety stocks, in
the upcoming chapters where we’ll cover the functionalities supported by those spe-
cific master data objects.
Next, we’ll cover the configuration for setting up and operating embedded PP/DS.
